## Libraries first!

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
```

## Ein paar (ausgedachte) Daten

```{r}
# Now create a couple of vectors, similar to
# the variables in the ALLBUS gender data.
(age <- c(52, 51, 32, 60, 76))
(sex <- factor(x = c("Mann", "Frau", "Frau", "Frau", "Frau"),
               levels = c("Mann", "Frau", "Divers")))
(eastwest <- factor(x = c("West", "West", "Ost", "West", "West"),
                    levels = c("West", "Ost")))
(incc <- c(2000, 1800, 950, 1300, 1300))
(id03 <- c(6, 6, 6, 5, 8))
```

## Data Frames

**Data frames** organize vectors of *equal length* along their indices.

```{r}
# Bind our 5 vectors along their index into a data frame.
# Assign that data frame to object "Dat".
(Dat <- data.frame(sex, age, eastwest, incc, id03))
```

## Tibbles 

```{r}
# Make Dat a tibble and assign it to object "Dat",
# (effectively overwriting Dat as a tibble).
(Dat <- as_tibble(Dat))
```


## Address single variables (The `$` operator)

```r
# Return variable "eastwest" contained in tibble Dat.
# (R for Data Science mentions two further commands.)
Dat$eastwest
```
